references.text: Gen 9:13 introduces the rainbow as a sign of the covenant between God and the earth, and is the immediate context for v.14 which describes when the rainbow will appear.
Gen 9:16 uses almost identical language about the rainbow in the cloud and explains that God will see it and remember the eternal covenant with all living things.
Isaiah 54:9 refers directly to God's promise to Noah never again to flood the earth, which connects to the rainbow as a sign confirming this covenant.
Ezekiel 1:28 compares the vision of God's glory to a rainbow in the cloud on a rainy day, a strong parallel to the rainbow as a covenant sign in Gen 9:14.
Revelation 4:3 describes a rainbow around God's throne, which can be seen as a symbol of God's faithfulness and the covenant promise given through the rainbow sign in Genesis 9.
Revelation 10:1 describes an angel with a rainbow over his head, possibly alluding to God's covenant faithfulness symbolized by the rainbow.
